- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply mean reversion to recent 5–7 day average.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +2–4% above true peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in cycle (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) and price is rising, model often fails to account for mean reversion; add 1–3% downward adjustment after 10–15 days.
